You will work at the intersection of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) strategy, data governance, and stakeholder engagement — contributing directly to the national ESG reporting framework for Singapore's public healthcare sector. We are seeking a Senior Assistant Director to lead the development of robust ESG data reporting systems and internal controls, and to prepare disclosures that meet global standards whilst aligning with national frameworks. Reporting to the Group Director of OSH, with matrix reporting to the Deputy Group Chief Financial Officer, you will work closely with Finance and Risk Management teams as well as institutional partners across SingHealth to ensure that sustainability data is accurate, meaningful, and audit-ready. What You Will Do: You will develop and implement a cluster-wide sustainability data collection system and internal controls framework, with the goal of establishing a validated, audit-ready baseline and enabling prospective tracking across all SingHealth institutions Working in close collaboration with the Finance and Risk Management teams, you will integrate financial and social metrics into ESG disclosures, ensuring consistency and alignment between SingHealth's Financial Report and its ESG report as part of the Ministry of Health (MOH)-led collective reporting for the public healthcare sector. You will coordinate with all SingHealth institutions to meet MOH-mandated milestones for data submission, managing timelines and escalating critical decisions to senior leadership where appropriate. You will regularly review and assess sustainability-related risks and opportunities, working with internal stakeholders to support prioritisation of action plans and track material ESG topics that align with SingHealth's mission, strategic goals, and commitments to the communities it serves. Insights drawn from tracked data will be shared in a timely manner to support care improvement and strategic transformation across the cluster. Supporting the SingHealth governance framework for sustainability, you will ensure transparency and accuracy in outcome reporting. You will also supervise one direct report to provide guidance and direction as the team's work matures. You'll architect and oversee the GAIMx Generative AI platform, bringing together multiple AI initiatives across SingHealth–Duke-NUS to create a robust, trusted, and scalable ecosystem that transforms clinical care and research. We are seeking an Assistant Director to design, build, and oversee the technical architecture of the GAIMx platform. You'll establish AI development best practices, lead the creation of reusable and secure AI components including domain-specific foundation models, and ensure interoperability across diverse healthcare systems whilst maintaining the highest standards of security and compliance. What You'll Do: You will lead the end-to-end development of the GAIMx solution, managing both internal and external technical development teams whilst mentoring engineering and data science teams in healthcare technology best practices. Additionally, you'll integrate diverse clinical, research, and operational systems through healthcare standards including Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources APIs, Health Level Seven version 2, openEHR, and Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model. Your responsibilities include designing architectures aligned with Zero Trust Security and National Institute of Standards and Technology frameworks, overseeing implementation of identity and access management, encryption, and security monitoring, whilst conducting periodic security risk assessments. You'll guide teams in microservices and API-driven architectures, lead engineering of data pipelines for healthcare data using technologies like Spark, Kafka, and Databricks, and partner with data scientists to deploy Generative AI and large language models in clinical workflows. jobs.jd: Posting Date: 24 Aug 2026. Closing on 07 Sep 2026. At MSE and our family of agencies – PUB, NEA, and SFA – we drive sustainability and resilience initiatives that improve the everyday lives of Singaporeans. As part of the MSE Family, you will be at the forefront of innovation, leading efforts to safeguard water resources, protect public health, and ensure food safety. Through partnerships across sectors, we tackle evolving challenges while fostering an inclusive, safe, and supportive workplace. Join us in shaping Singapore’s sustainable future and making a lasting impact on the everyday lives of generations to come. Climate change poses an asymmetrical challenge for Singapore – we contribute only around 0.1% of global carbon emissions, but will be disproportionately impacted by its effects. In Feb 2021, the Government launched the Singapore Green Plan 2030, a whole-of-nation movement to advance Singapore’s national agenda on sustainable development. In Oct 2022, Singapore announced that it would raise its national climate target to achieve net zero emissions by 2050. There is much work to be done to realise the climate aspirations of Singapore. The available mitigation options have trade-offs, and need to be considered in the context of the overall triple transition of carbon, energy and the economy. Your work will therefore revolve around carefully weighing trade-offs, whether that be in exploring new possibilities for Singapore or ensuring existing policies remain fit-for-purpose. Climate action is a priority for MSE, and is driven by the Energy & Climate Policy Division (ECPD). ECPD is MSE’s coordinating policy desk for issues overseen by the Inter-Ministerial Committee on Climate Change (IMCCC). ECPD drives policies relating to climate science, climate adaptation and climate mitigation, including issues such as carbon pricing, decarbonising Singapore’s economy, coastal protection, and reducing urban heat. You will join the Climate Mitigation team to help Singapore navigate an uneven and complex climate landscape, domestically and internationally. As part of the Climate Mitigation team within ECPD, you will work with a diverse range of stakeholders from the public sector (e.g. NCCS, MTI and various statutory boards), private sector and civil society on a whole-of-nation effort to mitigate climate change. Amongst many other issues, you will be: • Developing strategies to realise carbon abatement through adoption of a variety of low-carbon solutions,from scaling up international carbon markets to promoting energy efficiency nationally; • Reviewing the price of carbon; • Reviewing and strengthening NEA’s capabilities to support low-carbon strategies, e.g. those in relation to NEA’s role as the carbon tax administrator and the national carbon accounting authority; • Developing thought leadership for international climate mitigation issues (e.g. scaling up innovative financing models to facilitate the low-carbon transition) in partnership with IMCCC agencies; and • Supporting inter-agency efforts in driving the triple transition of carbon, energy and economy. We are looking for candidates who: • Can contribute constructively in inter-agency policy reviews, and translate policy intent into implementable frameworks for the statutory boards • Can think critically and handle uncertainty • Have strong analytical skills, and able to see both the bigger picture and fine details • Have strong written and spoken communication skills • Are able to work both independently and within a team, and can actively maintain strong working relationships across agency boundaries.
